candidates.description: These tokens represent consecutive three-digit numbers, primarily in the 190s, along with a Devanagari numeral for 19.
These tokens represent common character n-grams and subword fragments found in Hindi text.
This vector represents common subword fragments and prefixes from Hindi text.
This feature vector represents common Hindi verb roots, inflections, and auxiliary suffixes used to construct tense and aspect.
This vector is related to Sanskrit/Indic conjunct consonants and vowel-consonant combinations featuring the halant (virama) sign.
This feature vector activates on Hindi text segments containing the anusvara diacritic ( ं ).
This vector represents Hindi vowel signs, standalone vowels, and common conjunct consonant endings used in Devanagari script tokenization.
This vector represents sequential numbers or integer counting values, primarily clustered around the high 180s.
This vector represents Hindi vowel signs and dependent vowel modifiers used in conjunction with consonants.
This vector activates for common Hindi pronouns, adjectives, and modifiers related to size, comparison, and possession.
